account:
Today I have kept my appointments: the mill inspection, lunch at home, and council letters at the office. I have now arrived at the neighbour's cottage for three o'clock tea. The secretary says no council letters have arrived; I asked for enquiries and a report at half past four. At six I am due in the great hall for an authorized lighting inspection with the builder.

Something unusual seems to be circulating around the bakery. Several townspeople repeated news of a 'bridge or port change' there, naming the baker and neighbour as present. One report also said the baker carried a sack of bread. I do not know what change they meant or whether these repetitions are independent observations. I have not witnessed any bridge or port alteration myself. The neighbour may be able to clarify matters during tea.

There is also substantial bread business underway. The secretary's written report says freight supplied the baker with 24 emeralds and 72 wheat for an order of 200 loaves; the baker said another 528 wheat were needed, with delivery to the bakery storeroom and hauling to be arranged today. Earlier I overheard the baker say the bakery chest was empty and seek a bread settlement and thirty emeralds promised by the innkeeper. I heard a distant shout from the baker this afternoon but could not understand it. These facts suggest provisioning and payment arrangements involving the baker, freight, and innkeeper, but I cannot establish their purpose or connect them securely to the bakery rumours or tonight's lighting inspection.

My mill inspection established that the stall had 73 hay bales priced at two emeralds each. Delivery terms, commitments against that stock, and the supplier's identity remain unconfirmed. No town purchase has been authorized. I found no baker when I visited the bakery earlier. I suspect there is activity I have not yet understood, but I have no direct evidence of a secret gathering or wrongdoing.
